domain_description: Teaching students whose home language is not the language of instruction — the design moves that keep cognitive demand high while making the language accessible. Vocabulary tiering, sentence frames, language-demand analysis, sheltered-instruction protocols, and scaffolded task modification. Built on the Cummins BICS/CALP distinction, Echevarria/Vogt/Short's SIOP model, and Beck/McKeown/Kucan's tiered vocabulary work, with meta-analytic evidence from Cheung & Slavin, Goldenberg, and the broader EAL/ELL research tradition.

skills.description: Generate tiered sentence frames that let EAL students participate in academic discourse before they have fully independent academic language. Frames are scaffolds, not scripts: they expose the syntax and discourse markers of a subject, then fade as students take them over.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Oral language interventions strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Frames are paper or screen — no materials cost. The lift is teacher design time: building frames that match the discourse of the subject, tiering them across proficiency levels, and remembering to fade them as students internalise the patterns. EEF Oral language interventions strand carries +6 months on high-security evidence (154 studies); sentence frames are one well-established scaffold within that strand but have no clean standalone meta-analysis. The 2023 "over-framing" critique (Lemov et al.) is worth heeding — frames that are never faded become language restrictions rather than supports.

skills.description: Audit a classroom task through Cummins' BICS/CALP lens before students hit it — what vocabulary, syntax, discourse moves, and background knowledge the task assumes, and where EAL or multilingual learners will hit a barrier that is linguistic rather than cognitive. Use as a planning step that feeds into scaffolding decisions (sentence frames, vocabulary pre-teaching, task modification).
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Oral language interventions strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: No materials cost; the lift is teacher planning time. The honest framing: language demand analysis is a diagnostic precondition for effective scaffolding — not itself an intervention with a student-outcome meta-analysis. Cummins' BICS/CALP distinction (1979, refined 2008) is foundational theory rather than a tested intervention. The EEF Oral language interventions strand (+6 months, high evidence security) is the relevant umbrella because the downstream scaffolding decisions (frames, vocabulary pre-teaching, oral rehearsal) live there. Skip this step and you scaffold the wrong thing; do it well and the scaffolds that follow are aimed at the actual barriers, not assumed ones.

skills.description: Modify an existing classroom task so EAL learners can access it without losing the cognitive demand — the Walqui/Gibbons "high challenge, high support" principle. Add language scaffolds (frames, glossaries, visuals, oral rehearsal) that reduce the linguistic load while preserving the thinking the task was designed to require.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Oral language interventions strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: No materials cost; the lift is design judgment. The key risk this skill addresses: well-meaning scaffolding often quietly strips cognitive demand along with the language barrier — students end up doing an easier task in plain English instead of the original task with linguistic support. Walqui's "high challenge, high support" principle and Gibbons' work on scaffolding for ELLs ground the practice. Anchor: EEF Oral language interventions +6 months (high evidence security) — the scaffolds this skill produces (frames, visuals, rehearsal, glossaries) sit within that strand. The EAL-specific scaffolding literature is well-developed conceptually but lacks an isolated meta-analysis with a clean effect size; Belland et al. 2017 (computer-based scaffolding in STEM, g=0.46) shows the broader scaffolding principle holds but is not EAL-specific.
